photograph.author: Christian Fischer
photograph.description: The Chinese mitten crab , Eriocheir sinensis . This male specimen was found ashore in 150 metres distance to the banks of the Elbe river in the German federal state of Brandenburg . It behaves defending against the viewer by erecting the body and showing its hairy claws. The carapax’s width is estimated at six centimetres.
photograph.credit: Own work . Location: North-western Brandenburg, Germany.
photograph.mediaType: Reference photograph/micrograph; imaging and identification require individual review
photograph.review: Actual local retained photograph inspected October24, compared individually for shell profile, chela/leg structure, pigment and setae. No generative alteration.
photograph.changes: Resized inside 1000 px, flattened and JPEG encoded; no generative alteration.
photograph.captionLicense: External Commons description text; retain source page and its applicable license
photograph.identityScope: Christian Fischer caption identifies a defensive male on land near the Elbe. This is a selected dark adult male study, not proof of all color forms or a calibrated scan; the supported quiet/walking controls do not reproduce the source defensive display.

shape.before: The withheld generic oval/rod-limbed draft and its concrete shortcomings remain shown in the comparison sheet.
shape.changed: A convex rounded-quadrangular shell has four side teeth with a reduced fourth, four frontal teeth and a V-shaped median notch. Long eight-legged support, narrow pointed final legs, nearly equal hairy palms, white finger tips and a simplified male ventral cover replace the sparse generic draft.
shape.remaining: Shell outline, cristae, eye sockets, leg ratios and joint axes remain unmeasured. The hair field is an authored approximation without calibrated density or wetness. Maxillipeds, sternites, gills and pleopods are incomplete. The selected male photograph shows a defensive display; the supported study does not reproduce that display, burrowing or migration.

surface.changed: Dense attached short dark claw setae replace scattered hair rods. A smoother dark cuticle with restrained variation, paler limb undersides and distal leg fringes replaces uniform tan pigment.
surface.remaining: Original numerical illustration, not a scan, calibrated albedo, measured cuticle optics or full species variation. Shell outline, cristae, eye sockets, leg ratios and joint axes remain unmeasured. The hair field is an authored approximation without calibrated density or wetness. Maxillipeds, sternites, gills and pleopods are incomplete. The selected male photograph shows a defensive display; the supported study does not reproduce that display, burrowing or migration.

movement.changed: Same geometry and materials across a short authored lateral bout with planted support and lifted recovery, local chela/antennule handling, finger opening, quiet support and Observe reset. Eight pointed walking legs remain distinct from swimming paddles.
movement.remaining: No species-measured coordinates, biological frequency, joint limits, forces, fluid dynamics, sensory physiology, food contact or ingestion. No validated sleep, development, courtship or migration. Fixed-length/support tests are software consistency checks, not empirical biomechanics.

sourceAssessment: Selected Sakai2013 diagnosis printed1127 and actual frontal comparison figure1C printed1113 were inspected. Christian Fischer’s authentic male photo was viewed. GBIF accepted identity checked. Smithsonian NEMESIS description was available in an indexed excerpt; later direct full-page requests timed out. The separate SERC Watch page rejected direct retrieval/403; this failure remains disclosed.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Removed excessive coarse shell pigment after the first top-view inspection.
Confined toothed-margin deformation to the shell edge after final sheets exposed artificial radial specular folds; replaced all42 affected captures.
Distinguished Sakai2013 Paraeriocheir combination from the current retained Eriocheir species concept.
